title: Special Topics: Theory of Reinforcement Learning
weeklyTopics: Introduction to reinforcement learning; historical examples (Samuel's Checkers, AlphaGo)
Markov processes and Markov reward processes
Linear programming approach to solving MDPs; MLE of Markov processes; Hoeffding's inequality
The experts problem, Follow-the-Regularized-Leader, mirror descent
Stochastic multi-armed bandits (Explore-Then-Commit, UCB, Thompson Sampling)
Optimism-based algorithms for online RL in MDPs (UCRL2)

Advanced topics chosen by student interest: RL with function approximation, continuous state/action spaces (LQR), offline/off-policy evaluation, multi-task/transfer RL, hierarchical RL, multi-agent RL
Student paper-reading presentations on advanced RL topics
workloadNotes: PhD-level special topics seminar, taught remotely (COVID-19); no graded homeworks or exams; grades based on class presentations (student groups present papers on advanced RL topics) and a final project (proposal due partway through term).
prerequisitesText: Aimed at advanced graduate students in statistics, CS, control theory, and operations research; prior exposure to RL or at least MDPs strongly recommended; significant mathematical maturity expected.
textbooks: Sutton and Barto, Reinforcement Learning: An Introduction (2nd ed.)
Puterman, Markov Decision Processes: Discrete Stochastic Dynamic Programming
Hazan, Introduction to Online Convex Optimization
